newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares surge on Turk Telekom sale approval.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares surge on Turk Telekom sale approval.

text.p: Turkish shares soared further into record territory on Thursday after the constitutional court gave the green light for the sale of Turk Telekom, the centrepiece of the government's privatisation plans, analysts said.

The IMKB National-100 leapt 8.07 percent to close at its 15th all-time high this year of 1,352. Volume reached a record total of 43.46 trillion lira ($378 million) from a previous high of 35.89 trillion ($312 million).
Analysts and brokers said they expected the court ruling would further fuel the sustained rally, which has lifted the index by 38.5 percent since the start of the year.
The Turkish lira, which has weakened 6.6 percent against the dollar this year, was unchanged on Thursday at 115,000.
The court rejected most of a challenge by 116 opposition MPs to the privatisation after two-and-a-half days of talks.
"It is the best news we've had in more than a year," Salomon Brothers Turkey equities analyst Unal Kurtaran said.
"With this I think the government will be able to achieve most of its targets," he said.

The ruling, on top of the sale of two banks, tyre and cement factories and the leasing of port facilities has boosted the Islamist-led government's hopes of reaching a target of $5 billion from sell-offs this year, analysts said.
This figure does not include the $3.5 billion targeted from the sale of the state telecommunications company, which has been halted three times by the constitutional court since 1993.

The court on Thursday only cancelled a clause on the legal supervision of licence agreements for GSM mobile phone services by the Council of State, which will not effect plans to raise another $1 billion from GSM mobile phone service licences.
Some analysts and brokers warned that the buoyant market response to the court ruling may be reined in initially by a bout of profit-taking.
"The buying was very heavy and the rise was very sharp. So you can expect selling some time ahead," said Ata Securities analyst Murat Iman.

Turkey's Transport Minister Omer Barutcu signalled that the government would be cautious in its approach to the placement of Telekom shares considering the meteoric rise in stocks this year, which was primarily built on sell-off expectations.
"Ten percent will be issued to assess our market condition at that time," he said, noting that under the privatisation 49 percent of Telekom is aimed to be sold.
A Goldman Sachs-led consortium was last month appointed to advise on the sell-off, which the government is hoping to begin in the second-half of the year.

The potential of the market may be further tested by the government's plan to open tenders in the first-quarter for the partial sale of state refiner Tupras and petroleum products distributor Petrol Ofisi, analysts said.
But they said the government's commitment to pushing ahead with the plans was demonstrated by the zero-deficit budget approved for 1997, which programmes in huge sell-off revenues.
Market participants said the market uptrend will be sustained, but cautioned about the level of gains in some sectors.

"The rally will continue tomorrow but investors must be aware that some share prices have already risen too much," said Turgay Ozaner from Global Securities, who forecast the leading index would soon reach 1,500.
Largely state-owned firms such as flat steel maker Eregli and Turkish Airlines were among the most active shares on Thursday.
T-bill and bond yields rose by 2-3 points, with the average yield on the most heavily traded October 30, 1997 paper up 2.63 points to 89.55 percent.
($1=115,000 Turkish lira)
